angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,073,465 km at 33.35 pc = 0.43 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 29.9864 +/- 0.0205 mas (same row, RUWE 0.99): 33.35 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.543 +/- 0.01 solar radii from Heidari et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HD 88986 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...681A..55H/abstract): 1,073,465 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.25 +/- 0.05 solar masses from Heidari et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HD 88986 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...681A..55H/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5861 +/- 17 K from Heidari et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 88986 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...681A..55H/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Heidari et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 88986 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...681A..55H/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hd-88986.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.158, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
